results.label: aov_no_crypto
results.verdict: RETRACTED — was: ADMIT  (+11.25%)  +11.25% improvement, p=4.615e-07, n=5/5 — clears both significance and effect size

retracted.reason: RETRACTED 2026-11-04. Gated against a baseline measured 2h50m earlier (2026-11-03T19:37 local), under a different set of resident processes and a different machine state. The comparison described two different machine states rather than two configurations, so the effect it reports is not the effect of the AOV change. No statistical gate could have caught it: Welch's t-test on two independent series attributes the drift to the candidate, which is what 'independent' means. Re-measured 2026-11-04 with both arms alternately in one session (harness/levers.py, aov_variant lever, the beauty_only variant, which is the stronger of the two AOV reductions): +9.19% (p=8.6e-05). The no_crypto variant was not re-measured on 2026-11-04, so it has no replacement figure of its own; the measured AOV win on this workload is real but smaller than this pairing reported.
retracted.original_verdict: ADMIT  (+11.25%)  +11.25% improvement, p=4.615e-07, n=5/5 — clears both significance and effect size
retracted.replacement_verdict: no_crypto  -0.09%  n=5  drift -0.75%  spread 1.65%  contention 10  (no_crypto)  DENY — measured with the current harness

reason_corrected.reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-11-06 with the current harness, and the conclusion is unchanged: dropping the cryptomatte AOV on its own is worth NOTHING. Now DENY -0.09% (paired, n=5/5, baseline drift -0.75%, control spread 1.65%), where the earlier measurement said DENY +0.77% (drift +0.31%). The five paired differences are -0.79, +0.96, +1.00, -0.70 and -0.25 seconds - they change sign, which is what a lever that does nothing looks like. The measurement is now honest in the ways the earlier one was not: the ssim guardrail's bar is measured between two different renders rather than scored against itself, the drift gate sees a busy window anywhere in the run and not only end to end, every lever warms up, and a warm-up repetition is excluded from the series rather than being measured as if it were a real one. Superseded rather than deleted; its numbers stay readable. The two AOV reductions remain NOT interchangeable: beauty_only removes every extra pass and pays (+10.85%), and no_crypto alone does not.

replacement_history.verdict: DENY (+0.85%), paired, n=5, baseline drift +1.59% - the no_crypto variant is NOT a win on this workload
replacement_history.superseded_because: SUPERSEDES the 2026-11-04 16:07 figure (+0.85%, drift +1.59%). That measurement was taken while the card was contended - the drift gate recorded +1.59% and the per-rep contention check did not exist yet, so a WSL benchmark holding the card was invisible to it. Re-measured 2026-11-04 at 22:19 on a card verified idle by process identity (the WSL competitor was waited out and named), with both arms alternately in one session: DENY, +0.77% (paired, n=5/5, baseline drift +0.31%, cv 0.72%, zero contention events, ssim guardrail baseline 0.9966 vs candidate 0.9952). The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on a clean series: dropping the cryptomatte AOV is worth nothing here. The +11.25% this verdict reported was drift between sessions, not the effect of the change. The two AOV reductions are NOT equivalent - beauty_only IS a real win (+9.19%, p=8.6e-05) because it removes all the extra passes, while no_crypto alone is worth nothing.
